claims.text: The strongest repository source explicitly requires ascending merge, recursive and iterative implementations, and stack-space comparison; Java/API, node reuse, and tie stability are not source-proven.

Under the declared Java node-reuse contract, both implementations match an independent sorted-union oracle while preserving every input node exactly once; the recursive implementation can accumulate linear call depth while the iterative implementation retains constant auxiliary pointer state.

findings: Repository source explicitly requires ascending merge, recursive and iterative implementations, and stack-space comparison; node class, language, node reuse, and equal-key stability are not source-proven.
Candidate clearly labels Java, input-node reuse, finite acyclic inputs, and first-list tie preference as reference-contract choices rather than source facts.

Both implementations make the same local decision: the smaller current head must be the next output node; recursive state is stored in call frames while iterative state remains in a constant number of references.

Independent Java oracle validates recursive and iterative outputs across a generated cross-product including empty lists, duplicates and integer extremes, and verifies exact input-node identity reuse with no cycle.
The O(m+n) time, O(m+n) worst-case recursive call stack, and O(1) iterative auxiliary-space claims are consistent with the shown implementations; the answer avoids fabricated production experience.
